assembly_instructions: Abstract micro-architecture block diagram, not to physical scale — XiangShan's die is only a few mm² and the picosecond-scale signal paths cannot be drawn literally. Blocks are sized for legibility and all floor-standing blocks sit on the ground line (y=0). The pipeline flows along +X: the decoupled front end (a fast uBTB plus the TAGE/ITTAGE predictors -> FTQ -> instruction-fetch unit -> instruction buffer) occupies negative X; decode/rename/dispatch sit at the origin; the wide back end fans out along Z — integer datapath on the centre line, the floating-point datapath toward +Z, and the memory datapath toward -Z. Materials are colour-coded by block class: 'black composite' = predictor and fetch logic, 'white composite' = decode/rename/dispatch logic, 'dark anodized aluminum' = queues and buffers, 'brushed steel' = register files and the ROB, 'welded/forged steel' = functional units, 'glass display' = caches. The reorder buffer is modelled as a tall slab with three thin entry-bank slabs exploded directly above it, so its ~256-entry retirement array is legible rather than a solid block. Copper cylinders are explicit datapath buses along the front-end spine, the dispatch-to-issue path, the integer and FP writeback paths, and the L2->L3 path; remaining edges are logical connections. The integer multiplier/divider and the FP divide/sqrt unit are modelled as cylinders to distinguish the long-latency units from the box-shaped ALUs and FMA pipes. The multi-level cache hierarchy is parked at far +X with L1s closest to their clients and the shared L3 last.

info.japanese_name: 香山 RISC-Vプロセッサ（南湖世代）
info.summary: XiangShan is an open-source, high-performance out-of-order RISC-V processor core developed by the Institute of Computing Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The Nanhu generation is a six-wide superscalar core with a decoupled front end and a deep, multi-ported back end.
info.description: XiangShan implements the RV64GC ISA and is written in the Chisel hardware-construction language. Its front end is decoupled from fetch: a branch-prediction unit combining a fast uBTB first stage with TAGE-SC-L for conditional-branch direction and ITTAGE for indirect-branch targets drives a Fetch Target Queue, which in turn steers the instruction-fetch unit and L1 instruction cache; fetched bytes land in an instruction buffer ahead of decode, rename and dispatch. The back end is built from separate integer, memory and floating-point issue queues that read a multi-ported physical register file and feed many functional units — multiple integer ALUs, an integer multiplier, fused-multiply-add floating-point units, an FP divide/sqrt unit, and several load/store units. A large reorder buffer (around 256 entries in Nanhu) tracks every in-flight instruction for precise, in-order retirement, while the memory subsystem pairs load and store queues with a data TLB, an L1 data cache, a unified private L2 and a shared L3.
info.operator: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences (ICT, CAS) / Beijing Institute of Open Source Chip (BOSC)
info.contract_value: Open source — released under Mulan PSL v2 (no commercial contract)
info.status: Active development; Nanhu (南湖) released, Kunminghu (昆明湖) generation in progress

sources.title: Towards Developing High Performance RISC-V Processors Using Agile Methodology (MICRO 2022)

parts.name: Micro Branch Target Buffer (uBTB)
parts.role: Fast single-cycle first-stage predictor that supplies an immediate branch-target guess each cycle before the slower tagged predictors confirm or override it.

parts.name: TAGE-SC-L Direction Predictor
parts.role: Predicts the taken/not-taken direction of conditional branches using tagged geometric-history tables with a statistical corrector and loop predictor.

parts.name: ITTAGE Indirect Target Predictor
parts.role: Predicts the target address of indirect branches and returns using an indirect-target TAGE structure.

parts.name: Fetch Target Queue (FTQ)
parts.role: Buffers predicted fetch streams from the branch predictors and decouples prediction from the instruction-fetch pipeline.

parts.name: Instruction Fetch Unit (IFU)
parts.role: Reads cache lines indicated by the FTQ, aligns and pre-decodes instructions, and forwards them to the instruction buffer.

parts.name: L1 Instruction Cache
parts.role: Private first-level cache supplying instruction bytes to the fetch unit; refilled from the unified L2.

parts.name: Instruction Buffer (IBUF)
parts.role: Holds fetched instructions to smooth the rate mismatch between the front end and the decode stage.

parts.name: Decode Unit
parts.role: Decodes up to six RISC-V instructions per cycle into internal micro-operations.

parts.name: Register Rename Unit
parts.role: Maps architectural registers to physical registers to eliminate false dependencies and enable out-of-order execution.

parts.name: Dispatch Unit
parts.role: Allocates reorder-buffer entries and steers renamed micro-ops into the integer, memory and floating-point issue queues.

parts.name: Integer Issue Queue
parts.role: Holds integer micro-ops and wakes them for out-of-order issue to the integer functional units as operands become ready.

parts.name: Memory Issue Queue
parts.role: Holds load and store micro-ops and issues them to the load/store units in dependence order.

parts.name: Floating-Point Issue Queue
parts.role: Holds floating-point micro-ops and issues them to the FP functional units when their operands are ready.

parts.name: Integer Physical Register File
parts.role: Multi-ported physical register file supplying integer operands to, and collecting results from, every integer functional unit.

parts.name: Floating-Point Physical Register File
parts.role: Multi-ported register file holding floating-point operands and results for the FP datapath, feeding both FMA pipes and the FP divide unit.

parts.name: Integer ALU 0
parts.role: Single-cycle integer arithmetic and logic unit; also resolves branch conditions.

parts.name: Integer ALU 1
parts.role: Second single-cycle integer ALU, widening integer issue width.

parts.name: Integer ALU 2
parts.role: Third single-cycle integer ALU sustaining the wide superscalar back end.

parts.name: Integer Multiplier / Divider
parts.role: Pipelined multiplier and iterative divider handling long-latency integer operations; cylindrical body distinguishes it from the single-cycle ALUs.

parts.name: Floating-Point FMA Unit 0
parts.role: First fused multiply-add pipe executing IEEE-754 floating-point multiply-add arithmetic.

parts.name: Floating-Point FMA Unit 1
parts.role: Second fused multiply-add pipe, doubling floating-point multiply-add issue width per cycle.

parts.name: Floating-Point Divide / Sqrt Unit
parts.role: Iterative floating-point divide and square-root unit handling long-latency FP operations off the FMA pipes; cylindrical body marks it as the long-latency FP unit.

parts.name: Data TLB (DTLB)
parts.role: Translates virtual load/store addresses to physical addresses for the memory pipelines, caching recent page-table entries.

parts.name: Load/Store Unit 0
parts.role: Generates addresses and executes memory accesses, performing store-to-load forwarding through the load/store queues.

parts.name: Load/Store Unit 1
parts.role: Second memory pipeline, doubling load/store throughput per cycle.

parts.name: Reorder Buffer (ROB)
parts.role: Tracks every in-flight instruction in program order and retires results in order, providing precise exceptions and recovery; its ~256-entry array is shown exploded in the three banks stacked above it.

parts.name: ROB Entry Bank 0 (exploded)
parts.role: Exploded view: first slice of the ROB's ~256-entry circular array, lifted clear of the slab to reveal that the retirement backbone is a banked entry table rather than a solid block.

parts.name: ROB Entry Bank 1 (exploded)
parts.role: Exploded view: second slice of the ROB entry array; each bank holds head/tail pointers and per-instruction status bits used to drive in-order commit.

parts.name: ROB Entry Bank 2 (exploded)
parts.role: Exploded view: top slice of the ROB entry array; the stacked banks show the buffer is multi-banked so several instructions can be allocated and retired per cycle.

parts.name: Load Queue
parts.role: Holds in-flight loads, detecting memory-ordering violations against later stores.

parts.name: Store Queue
parts.role: Buffers committed-pending stores and forwards their data to dependent loads before they drain to the cache.

parts.name: L1 Data Cache
parts.role: Private first-level data cache serving the load/store units; refilled from the unified L2.

parts.name: Unified L2 Cache
parts.role: Private unified second-level cache backing both L1 caches and connecting to the shared L3.

parts.name: Shared L3 Cache
parts.role: Large last-level cache shared across cores, the final on-chip stop before main memory.

parts.name: Fetch Datapath Bus
parts.role: Copper datapath bus carrying fetched instruction bytes from the fetch unit to the instruction buffer.

parts.name: Decode Feed Bus
parts.role: Copper bus delivering buffered instructions from the instruction buffer to the decode unit.

parts.name: Decode-to-Rename Bus
parts.role: Copper bus carrying decoded micro-ops from decode to register rename.

parts.name: Rename-to-Dispatch Bus
parts.role: Copper bus carrying renamed micro-ops from rename into the dispatch stage.

parts.name: Dispatch-to-Issue Bus
parts.role: Copper bus distributing dispatched micro-ops from the dispatch unit into the issue queues.

parts.name: Issue-to-Register-File Bus
parts.role: Copper bus connecting the integer issue queue to the multi-ported physical register file.

parts.name: FP Issue-to-Register-File Bus
parts.role: Copper bus connecting the floating-point issue queue to the FP physical register file.

parts.name: Integer Writeback-to-ROB Bus
parts.role: Copper writeback bus carrying integer functional-unit results back to the reorder buffer for retirement.

parts.name: FP Writeback-to-ROB Bus
parts.role: Copper writeback bus carrying floating-point FMA and divide results back to the reorder buffer for retirement.

parts.name: L2-to-L3 Cache Bus
parts.role: Copper bus linking the private unified L2 cache to the shared L3 cache.
